newsitem.title: USA: Frigid temperatures linger in Midwest, Washington.
newsitem.headline: Frigid temperatures linger in Midwest, Washington.

text.p: Deepfreeze conditions that have held the Midwest in a weeklong grip lingered Saturday, with temperatures stuck in the single digits.

By nightfall temperatures were expected to dip below zero again, but arctic air was moving eastward out of Nebraska, signaling a moderating trend, forecasters said. No relief was seen until midweek, however.
In Chicago, the thermometer registered a nippy 5 degrees Fahrenheit (-15 C).

Most of Wisconsin was in a range of 3 degrees (-16 C) to 9 degrees Fahrenheit (-12 C), while Michigan averaged 10 degrees Fahrenheit. Minnesota's temperatures were similar, and some western parts of the state were experiencing a light snow.

Warmer air was trying to work its way into the frigid Midwest, chasing the cold air, said meterologist Vinnie Moise. "As a result... some light snow could result Sunday in Chicago, most of Indiana, Wisconsin and Michigan," he said.
If the current wind pattern continues, winter's bite could amelioriate somewhat with the return of above-normal temperatures of about 29 degrees F.
In Washington, the 53rd U.S. presidental inaugural festivities began in bone-chilling cold that checked the size of crowds attending events on the national Mall.
Event organizers erected seven "heated" tents that for the most part were only slightly warmer than outside, mainly because the white canvas at least cut down the wind.
The National Weather Service said temperatures were expected to remain in the teens (-7 to -10 Celsius) for most of the day, and cautioned that wind-chill factors made it feel much worse.
At the food tents, workers wearing hoods and earmuffs served their patrons.
The loneliest man at the American Kitchen tent was Drew Shack of Columbia, Maryland. The lemon snow-cones he was selling had no takers.
"It's warmer in my freezer than it is in the tent," he said. "I'm serious. The freezer's set at 32 degrees (0 Celsius). It's 26 (-3 Clesius) in the tent."
"You take it out and it freezes like a rock," he said.
